brief: A display stand with the large platform on a spike where three bases meet.

requirements.evidence: Three full bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full) form a cluster with a raised spike platform as the display surface; capped and joint-bolted via capOpenFaces and lockJoints.

requirements.requirement: The large platform on a spike
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 with setSpikeAccessory accessory platform-lrg (51.96x60mm large platform, not the 22.95mm small one).
Spike junction is [{0,0},{0,1},{1,0}] — exactly the three bases placed around that corner; check_build ok, meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a three-base hexagonal cluster (0,0 / 1,0 / 0,1 at level 0), placed a mount spike at their shared junction, and trapped the large platform (platform-lrg) on it as a display stand. Applied house rules capOpenFaces and lockJoints; check_build passes with meshClash clear. No display prop was added because find_surfaces returned no surface for the spike platform and a prop cannot rest on a spike, so the platform itself is left clear to show the display surface.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Display stand with a large spike platform — I'll set three bases around a junction and mount the platform there.
